canh-phuc-cung-phi-ngu: A brand-new painting of a natural, lived-in, richly furnished room, painted exactly like image 1 (the bedroom): same hand, same brushwork, same soft painterly finish, same natural warm colours, saturation and contrast, same depth with furniture, curtains and objects arranged through the whole room from the foreground to the back. Wide panoramic, eye-level view, summer morning. ROOM: Cảnh Phúc cung chính điện bedroom, the private bedchamber of the imperial consort who heads this palace in ancient China, a real room in daily use: dark rosewood pillars and beams, carved lattice windows at the back opening onto a sunny courtyard garden with a tree and a lotus pond, a carved wooden partition with a round moon-gate opening; at the centre of the room, the large clear main subject, one larger canopy bed of carved rosewood with soft purple gauze curtains tied back with tassels and purple silk brocade bedding embroidered with crabapple blossoms, more carving and jade-green inlay on the bed frame; around it a carved dressing table with a large bronze mirror, a lacquered jewellery cabinet and jade ornaments, a carved screen painted with crabapple blossoms, round stools with purple cushions, hanging palace lanterns with purple tassels, a clothes stand with a purple silk robe, porcelain vases of crabapple branches, a tea table with a fine tea set, a shelf with jade and porcelain treasures, a small incense burner, slippers on the floor. Cảnh Phúc cung signature style, the same in every room of this palace: crabapple blossoms (hải đường) are its flower, painted on the screens, embroidered on the silks and in the vases; motifs of bats among auspicious clouds carved in the beams and furniture; dark rosewood with jade-green inlay and jade ornaments; round-backed rosewood furniture; a round moon-gate opening in a carved partition. PHI level, clearly richer than a Tần: deeper carving, rich jade-green inlay, gilt edging on the furniture, silk brocade, many jade and porcelain treasures. The soft purple accent colour is woven through the bedding, curtains and cushions. No phoenix anywhere (no phoenix carving, embroidery, figure or pendant), no imperial yellow, no golden-yellow fabrics. The bottom-right corner nearest the viewer stays almost clear, holding at most one small object; tea tables and stools stand further back in the room.
